item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would review and merge after a small correction. It adds only the requested Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves Add, and keeps FilesOption behavior unchanged. A makes broad, explicitly forbidden API and retry changes.","reasons":["B implements the exact requested Upload signature and encodes field \"file\" with the supplied filename using internal/multipartbody.NewFile.","B keeps the change narrowly focused and preserves the existing Add implementation and FilesOption machinery.","B tests multipart field/name/content and verifies that the complete multipart upload survives a 429 retry.","A explicitly violates the contract by adding association options and multipart fields, introducing NewFileWithFields, and modifying unrelated RawClient request/retry and body-closing behavior globally although the contract forbids those changes and requires Add behavior to remain unchanged independently of Upload tests. As required by the contract, Upload should simply call s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...) after constructing the replayable multipart body. This is a localized and reviewable correction compared with A's broader divergence."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request, decoding, and error logic.","Adds multiple public association APIs and changes FilesOption internals despite the explicit prohibition on association fields and additional convenience APIs.","Refactors global RawClient body replay, Content-Length, and ownership semantics outside the requested scope, materially changing Add and other endpoints such as Raw.Do and Update. It also uses a new multipart helper rather than the required NewFile path."],"risks_b":["Upload incorrectly calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating option handling, decoding, and missing-data behavior.","Tests do not cover empty-filename and nil-content validation or propagation of source-reader failures.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than demonstrating buffering and retry from a one-shot or file-backed source reader."]}
